cuts.item: four school-related capital items (removed from FY26 capital plan, to be pursued in FY27)

statements.statement: The chair told a State House committee this year's school budget gap is far larger than last year's, representing a stated share of the school budget.
The chair said an override the prior year closed a stated gap in the school budget.
The chair said the town decided against seeking another override this year because residents are already financially stretched.
The chair told legislators a Chapter 70 inflation adjustment would bring Lunenburg additional funding.
The chair said increased in-district transportation funding from the state would bring additional funding.
The chair said an increased special education circuit breaker reimbursement would bring additional funding.
The chair said a proposed 'whole child grant' program would bring additional funding.
Four FY26 school capital items were removed from the capital plan and replaced with local match funding for a heat pump project tied to a green communities grant.

warnings.prediction: Each year departments will keep fighting over an increasingly small share of funding, pitting town departments against each other.

warnings.about: a future override for capital projects
warnings.condition: if the municipal building and Marshall Park debt exclusions are approved amid market volatility
warnings.prediction: The town may need to seek another override next year given the scale of proposed capital borrowing and uncertain economic conditions.

warnings.about: the primary school heat pump/green communities capital swap
warnings.condition: if bid prices exceed the current estimate
warnings.prediction: If bids for the primary school heat pump/control system come back significantly higher than estimated, funding for other capital requests could be jeopardized.
A four-year delay in the municipal building project would produce a project about 20% smaller for the same money, which a committee member said would make the project no longer viable.
